question: A pure silicon crystal is doped separately with phosphorus and aluminium. Predict the type of semiconductor formed in each case and justify your answer.

options.A:
Phosphorus-doped silicon
It forms p-type silicon with holes as majority carriers.
Aluminium-doped silicon
It forms n-type silicon with electrons as majority carriers.
options.B:
Phosphorus-doped silicon
Phosphorus is pentavalent and donates a weakly bound fifth electron, so it forms n-type silicon with electrons as majority carriers.
Aluminium-doped silicon
Aluminium is trivalent and creates holes, so it forms p-type silicon with holes as majority carriers.
options.C:
Phosphorus-doped silicon
It remains intrinsic because phosphorus has four valence electrons.
Aluminium-doped silicon
It becomes an insulator with no carriers.
options.D:
Phosphorus-doped silicon
It forms p-type silicon because phosphorus accepts electrons.
Aluminium-doped silicon
It forms n-type silicon because aluminium donates free electrons.
